contracts: Downloads, page JavaScript/beforeunload message bodies and shared scene modal bodies use the Rust-owned viewport in the opt-in backend. Views retains its original bounded ScrollView policy and dialog appearance.

Rust owns viewport extent/allocation, height clipping, wrapping-width reservation, authoritative offset, reveal/clamp and top/bottom overflow geometry/visibility. Native content measurements, separator paint, platform scrollbar/events/AX, window/frame/focus/IME and per-control View identities remain adapters.
Dialog background uses the live dialog color token, including the content layer. Shared modal bodies retain the native 2px top/bottom layout workaround and provider-specific maximum height.

Scene callbacks use weak lifetime bindings instead of native ScrollView synchronization/subscriptions. Shared modal refresh closure is owned by the viewport, points to its owned content subtree, and is never posted with unretained state. Download/profile and page/dialog teardown cases cover closure/editor lifetimes.

Native oracle checks bounded preferred size, wrapping allocation, offsets and overflow separators at multiple sizes and both themes. Existing download and page dialog scene/AX/Cocoa/close/profile cases retain their assertions through the common interface.
No browser service, stores, policy/admission/validation or persistence behavior changed. No dependency added.
limits: Full automated tests do not establish complete functional/manual/release parity.
